interpretations: Join fees to matching orders and users, group by `fees.orderslink` and `users.acctscope`, and average non-null `feerate` values for each pair. Compute the global mean of those pair averages, keep pairs strictly above it, calculate each excess, and use `RANK()` within each account scope in descending excess order. Return pairs with rank ≤ 3, with the requested values unrounded
queries:
WITH pair_averages AS (
    SELECT
        f.orderslink,
        u.acctscope,
        AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate
    FROM fees AS f
    JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
    JOIN users AS u ON u.userstamp = o.userlink
    WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope
),
global_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_feerate) AS mean_feerate
    FROM pair_averages
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        p.orderslink,
        p.acctscope,
        p.avg_feerate,
        p.avg_feerate - g.mean_feerate AS excess,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY p.acctscope
            ORDER BY p.avg_feerate - g.mean_feerate DESC
        ) AS rank
    FROM pair_averages AS p
    CROSS JOIN global_mean AS g
    WHERE p.avg_feerate > g.mean_feerate
)
SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 3
